name: Arithmetic series (sum)
description: Computes the sum of the first n terms of an arithmetic sequence with first term a1 and common difference d, as n over two times the quantity two a1 plus (n minus 1) d. The result is the running total of those terms.
notes: The number of terms n should be a positive integer. Equivalently this is n times the average of the first and last terms; a negative d can make the sum decrease.

name: Geometric series (sum)
description: Computes the sum of the first n terms of a geometric series with first term a1 and common ratio r, using a1×(1−r^n)/(1−r). It totals a1 + a1·r + a1·r² and so on up to n terms.
notes: This formula requires r not equal to 1; if r equals 1 the sum is simply a1×n. The exponent n is the number of terms, not the last term index.

name: Infinite geometric series (sum)
description: Computes the sum of an infinite geometric series a1 + a1·r + a1·r² + … as a1/(1−r). The infinitely many terms converge to this finite value when the ratio is small enough in magnitude.
notes: The series converges only when the absolute value of r is less than 1; otherwise the sum does not exist. As r approaches 1 the total grows without bound.

name: Sum of first n integers
description: Computes the sum of the first n positive integers, 1 + 2 + ... + n, using the closed form n*(n+1)/2. It gives the total directly without adding the terms one by one.
notes: n should be a positive integer. The product n*(n+1) is always even, so the result is a whole number. These sums are the triangular numbers.

name: Sum of first n squares
description: Computes the sum of the first n squares, 1^2 + 2^2 + ... + n^2, using the closed form n*(n+1)*(2*n+1)/6. It gives the total directly from n alone.
notes: n should be a positive integer. The product n*(n+1)*(2*n+1) is always divisible by 6, so the result is a whole number. These are the square pyramidal numbers.

name: Sum of first n cubes
description: Computes the sum of the first n cubes, 1^3 + 2^3 + ... + n^3, using the closed form (n*(n+1)/2)^2. Notably this equals the square of the sum of the first n integers.
notes: n should be a positive integer. The result is always a perfect square, since it is the square of the nth triangular number n*(n+1)/2.

name: Sum of first n odd numbers
description: Computes the sum of the first n odd numbers, 1 + 3 + 5 + ... + (2n-1), which equals exactly n^2. Adding consecutive odd numbers always produces a perfect square.
notes: n should be a positive integer and counts how many odd numbers are summed, not the largest odd number. The result n^2 is always a perfect square.

name: Geometric series sum
description: Computes the sum of the first n terms of a geometric series with first term a and common ratio r, using a*(1 - r^n)/(1 - r). Each term is r times the previous one.
notes: This form requires r not equal to 1; if r equals 1 the sum is simply a*n. n is the number of terms and should be a positive integer.

name: Sum of Arithmetico-Geometric Series (Σk·r^k)
description: Computes the sum of the first n terms of the series Σk·r^k (k = 1 to n), a product of an arithmetic sequence (k) and a geometric sequence (r^k). The result represents the total sum of this arithmetico-geometric series.
notes: Requires r ≠ 1, since the closed-form derivation divides by (1−r)². When r = 1 the sum simplifies to n(n+1)/2 and must be computed separately.

name: Antiderivative of 1/(a²+x²)
description: Computes the value of the antiderivative (1/a)·arctan(x/a) for the standard integral ∫dx/(a²+x²), evaluated at a given x. The result represents the indefinite integral's value up to an arbitrary constant of integration.
notes: Requires a ≠ 0. To obtain a definite integral, evaluate this expression at the upper and lower bounds and subtract the results.

name: Antiderivative of 1/√(a²−x²)
description: Computes the value of the antiderivative arcsin(x/a) for the standard integral ∫dx/√(a²−x²), evaluated at a given x. The result represents the indefinite integral's value, expressed in radians, up to an arbitrary constant of integration.
notes: Requires a > 0 and |x| ≤ a (equivalently |x/a| ≤ 1) for the result to be real-valued.

name: Antiderivative of √(a²−x²)
description: Computes the value of the antiderivative of √(a²−x²), a standard result used to derive the area under a circular or elliptical arc. The result represents the indefinite integral's value at a given x, up to an arbitrary constant.
notes: Requires a > 0 and |x| ≤ a for real-valued results; this antiderivative underlies the derivation of the area of a circle via ∫√(a²−x²)dx.

name: Antiderivative of √(x²+a²)
description: Computes the value of the antiderivative of √(x²+a²), a standard result used in arc-length calculations and hyperbolic-related integrals. The result represents the indefinite integral's value at a given x, up to an arbitrary constant.
notes: Requires a ≠ 0; the logarithmic term is well-defined for all real x since x + √(x²+a²) is always positive.

name: Sum of Squares 1 to n (Closed Form)
description: Computes the sum of the squares of the integers from 1 to n using the closed form n(n+1)(2n+1)/6. It replaces adding 1^2 + 2^2 + ... + n^2 term by term.
notes: The index n should be a positive integer. The numerator is always divisible by 6, so the result is an exact whole number.

name: Sum of Cubes 1 to n (Closed Form)
description: Computes the sum of the cubes of the integers from 1 to n as the square of the nth triangular number, (n(n+1)/2)^2. This reflects the identity that the sum of cubes equals the square of the sum.
notes: The index n should be a positive integer. The result equals (1+2+...+n) squared, a perfect square.

name: Sum of First n Fourth Powers
description: Computes the sum of the fourth powers of the integers from 1 to n using the closed form n(n+1)(2n+1)(3n^2+3n-1)/30. It replaces adding 1^4 + 2^4 + ... + n^4 directly.
notes: The index n should be a positive integer. The numerator is always divisible by 30, so the exact result is a whole number.

name: Sum of the First n Odd Integers
description: Returns the sum of the first n odd integers (1 + 3 + 5 + ... ), which equals n squared. Adding the first n odd numbers always produces a perfect square.
notes: Here n is the count of odd terms summed, not the largest odd number. The result is exactly n^2 for any positive integer n.

name: Sum of First n Even Numbers
description: Returns the sum of the first n even integers (2 + 4 + 6 + ... ), which equals n(n+1). It is twice the nth triangular number.
notes: Here n is the count of even terms summed. The result equals n(n+1), always an even number for positive integer n.

name: Arithmetic Series Sum (First and Last Term)
description: Sums an arithmetic series of n terms by averaging the first and last terms and multiplying by the number of terms: n(a+l)/2. It works for any arithmetic progression whose endpoints are known.
notes: It requires the series to be arithmetic (constant difference) and needs the actual last term l, not the common difference. All n terms must lie between a and l.

name: Finite Geometric Series Sum (First n Terms)
description: Sums the first n terms of a geometric series with first term a and common ratio r using a(1-r^n)/(1-r). It gives the total of a + ar + ar^2 + ... + ar^(n-1).
notes: The ratio r must not equal 1, or the formula divides by zero; for r = 1 the sum is simply n times a. For |r| below 1 and large n the sum approaches a/(1-r).
